reason: 'The study doesn't say what it is, so I'm making it up' (question 36). Aron et al. 1997 published all 36 questions in an appendix, including the last one (source: Wikipedia, Arthur Aron).

Sadie's tRNA card reads AUG and carries methionine, and it pairs with an mRNA stake reading UAC. Methionine's codon on the mRNA is AUG, read by a tRNA with anticodon UAC; an mRNA codon UAC codes for tyrosine, not methionine.
'Seven across... Four letters, period of decline.' 'Decay,' said Olivier. 'Decay' has five letters, not four, and the story leaves it uncorrected as the last line.
uncertain: a doctor calls a mild illness a 'slow virus'; the medical term usually means serious long-incubation infections.

The story calls 289 g of NH3 from 51 g of H2 'impossible' and calls grams-to-moles-then-2/3 the error, then has Chase tell the class 'our answers are wrong'. 51 g H2 is about 25.5 mol, which gives 17 mol NH3, about 289 g. That answer is correct, and the product can outweigh the hydrogen because the nitrogen adds mass.
'He divided. Six point two percent, almost exactly.' $171 minus $152.06 is $18.94, which is about 11% of $171. Social Security at 6.2% would be $10.60.

The story says Chapter 7 of Pride and Prejudice has 'seventeen' servant appearances, two of them named (later it says 'twenty-five'). Chapter 7 mentions a servant about three times (footman and messengers), and none is named (source: Project Gutenberg text).

The story presents a thrust stage as one where everything faces one way and the audience sits 'in one place', a room with a front. A thrust stage has the audience on three sides; the one-directional stage described is a proscenium.

'Methionine, valine, proline, stop. A four-piece protein.' That is three amino acids, because the stop codon UAA adds none. Also, splitting CCAAUGGUACCGUAA from the first letter gives CCA AUG GUA CCG UAA, not the CAA UGG... frame the story attributes to 'the very first letter'.

'the artery the European Frida clamped shut with her own fingers' (repeated as 'the clamp of her own fingers'). In The Two Fridas she holds surgical forceps (hemostat) to stop the bleeding (source: Wikipedia, The Two Fridas). Also uncertain: the sky is described as stormy left, calm right. Megan's uncorrected guess that Kahlo was in her twenties is also wrong: the painting is from 1939, when she was 31-32.

The worked answer: 15.0 g Al with excess Br2 gives 'one hundred forty-seven grams' of AlBr3. 0.556 mol times 266.7 g/mol is about 148 g. Also, the sandwich analogy says two slices of bread make two sandwiches, when two slices make one.
'Elizabeth... could refuse Darcy twice.' Elizabeth refuses Darcy only once (Hunsford) and accepts his second proposal (source: Project Gutenberg text, ch. 58).
'twelve twelve-year-olds... the association had given her the Bantam house team'. Bantam is the 13-14 (U15) division; twelve-year-olds play Peewee (source: Wikipedia, Minor ice hockey).

For a thrown ball's height h(t), 'the right end beat her critical point', with the ball 'still climbing'. A thrown ball's height is a downward parabola, so an interior critical point is the global maximum and no endpoint can exceed it. The ball also cannot still be climbing after its peak.

'the small dark shape suspended at the painter's throat, its wings folded, its body slack'. In the painting the dead hummingbird hangs stiff with its wings outstretched like a pendant (source: Wikipedia, Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird). Also uncertain: the story describes leaves strung through the thorns.
'Sixty-one dollars and change for eight hours... which worked out to $7.25 an hour.' 8 x $7.25 = $58.00, and $61 over 8 hours is about $7.65 an hour.

'Twenty by ten... a hundred square feet', presented as the maximum for length plus width equal to 60. 20 x 10 is 200, not 100. With L + W = 60 the maximum area is at 30 by 30 (900 sq ft), and 20 by 10 does not even total 60.

The story says Owen swapped assertEquals's arguments and that swapping them back turned the test green. His call assertEquals(0, getYear()) already had expected first; the bug was a wrong expected value. Swapping argument order never changes whether assertEquals passes, it only changes the failure message.
